errors: No mathematical errors; the page is programmatic. Minor point: the self-duality of H_DR for smooth proper X needs X equidimensional (or a componentwise statement). This is implicit.

ideas.what: Poincaré duality, Gysin maps, cycle classes and functorialities for algebraic de Rham cohomology of smooth proper varieties, modelled on the Hodge-cohomology case
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic de Rham cohomology as a Weil cohomology (duality, cycle class map)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (1966 letter/IHES paper on de Rham cohomology); Hartshorne 1975
ideas.where_published: Sém. Bourbaki exp. 149 (1957) for the Hodge-cohomology version; 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (Publ. IHES 29, 1966); Crystals (Dix exposés, 1968)

ideas.what: Desire for an f^!, f_! formalism à la Residues and Duality for separated finite type morphisms, with de Rham-type coefficients
ideas.modern_name: Six-functor formalism for algebraic de Rham cohomology / D-modules
ideas.where_published: Programmatically in Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes (1968) and in Récoltes et Semailles (six operations, coefficients)

ideas.what: Such a duality should give singular homology algebraically (de Rham homology)
ideas.modern_name: Algebraic de Rham homology; Borel–Moore homology via f^!
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hartshorne 1975; Herrera–Lieberman; Bloch–Ogus 1974 (axiomatic Poincaré duality theories)
ideas.where_published: The 'papiers bleus' mentioned are not identified; Hartshorne 1975 acknowledges Grothendieck's ideas

ideas.what: Extend Grothendieck duality from complexes with O-linear differentials to complexes whose differentials are differential operators
ideas.modern_name: Duality for complexes of differential operators (Ω-modules / D-modules, Saito's correspondence between D-complexes and differential complexes)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Herrera–Lieberman 1971; Hartshorne 1975; M. Saito (1989) on induced D-modules and differential complexes

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly sets the task of extending the Residues-and-Duality f^! formalism from O-linear complexes to complexes with differential-operator differentials, as a unified coefficient theory. This was later achieved piecemeal (Herrera–Lieberman, Hartshorne, D-modules) rather than as he framed it. The idea itself is broadly known as his programme.
missed.quote: Il y aurait lieu en particulier d'étendre ce formalisme, du cas de complexes à différentielles linéaires, au cas des complexes [à] différentielles des op. différentiels.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This documents early (1967) priority for the idea that de Rham homology and six operations should come from Grothendieck duality applied to differential complexes. That is relevant to crediting the origins of algebraic de Rham homology and D-module duality, but it is not a new mathematical result.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a programmatic page restating a well-known Grothendieck aim: six operations for de Rham or crystalline coefficients, with de Rham homology via duality. It has been realized and largely credited (Hartshorne 1975 cites Grothendieck's ideas). The only new details are the explicit mention of the 'papiers bleus' and the precise formulation in terms of extending duality to differential-operator complexes.
transcription_corrections: 'classe de coh. associée à un cycle Λq [?]' — likely 'associée à un cycle Z' (or Z^q); the symbol is not Λ.
In the inserted phrase the crossed-out word is probably 'presque propres', leaving 'séparés de type fini' as the final reading; the transcription is consistent with this.
'(Springer)' after 'Hartshorne' refers to Residues and Duality, LNM 20.
'cohomologie de Hodge' refers to the Hodge-cohomology part of his Sém. Bourbaki exposé (probably exp. 149, 1957).
